about: Limits for release builds on CI's runners (omui-bench --check). Each says why it is there; raising one needs the same.

budgets.name: motion/drive-1000
budgets.why: interactive mode is the Set it is built on: 1000 driven springs a frame, measured beside motion/set-1000 (0.046 vs 0.048 ms p95 locally); a frame's share for a thousand UI channels

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-256
budgets.why: first scalar reference budget: 256x256 cells, 3 channels, 3 rules and cardinal neighbors; no GPU or Noita-scale claim

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-256
budgets.why: prepared rules and caller-owned fields; the tiled step reuses storage

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-present
budgets.why: D-132: a step's changed tiles (12 of 1024) recoloured and named in the field's image — 0.044 ms p95 locally; a frame's share for a 1024x1024 field whose front moves

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-present-all
budgets.why: D-132 worst case: every cell of 1024x1024 recoloured (2.7 ms p95 locally, 2.6 ns a cell); bounds a load or a palette change

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-frame
budgets.why: D-132: one DrawImage for the whole field, damage of the changed tiles' rows and the incremental CPU raster (0.52 ms p95 locally, 132 of 1024 rows)

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-step-sparse
budgets.why: D-167: a 1024x1024 field pays for what is awake — a fire's front in 32 of 1024 tiles is 2.0 ms p95 in a debug build locally, where every tile run (simulation/cellular-1024-step) is 69 ms; a frame's share with room for a runner

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-step-sparse
budgets.why: D-167: the tiles' bytes are the caller's; a sparse step allocates nothing

budgets.name: simulation/cellular-1024-rest
budgets.why: D-167: a field wholly at rest costs its tiles' bytes looked at and no cell (0.011 ms p95 in a debug build locally)

budgets.name: simulation/matter-reference-4096
budgets.why: D-165: the reference step's working space is kept between steps (matter::Workspace); a step with no events kept allocates nothing

budgets.name: simulation/matter-reference-4096
budgets.why: D-165: the laws on any carrier, 4096 instances each beside four — 2.4 ms p95 in a debug build locally (550 ns an instance); the reference a carrier's own path is held to, not the path a large world runs (the lattice's program, T1.7)

budgets.name: simulation/matter-lattice-4096
budgets.why: D-167: the lattice's step allocates nothing, with a table and reactions as with rules

budgets.name: simulation/matter-lattice-4096
budgets.why: T1.7: the same world as simulation/matter-reference-4096 by the lattice's own path, the same bits — 2.3 ms p95 in a debug build locally (550 ns a cell, the reference's cost: the scalar step reads the program's words a cell at a time); what a large world pays is the tiles awake (below) and the device's kernel (T1.8)

budgets.name: simulation/matter-256-causes
budgets.why: D-169: what watching a field of matter costs — the same world as simulation/matter-lattice-256-sparse stepped as an agent's subject, its record of causes made at each commit: 18.6 ms p95 in a debug build locally against 17.8 ms a step unwatched (0.6 ms: where each cell of the tiles awake came from, each against itself a step ago; the kernel's `why` only where something happened — 3 allocations a step on average, none where nothing did). A first bound: the sparse step's and a fifth

budgets.name: simulation/matter-1024-sparse
budgets.why: M6.1: a 1024x1024 world of the standard matter on the CPU within a 60 Hz frame — a lake at rest, sand pouring, wood alight, lava by water, 10% of the cells awake — stepped sparsely in pieces on the shared pool (Execution::parallel) and checked to be the bits of one after another: 7.0 ms p95 in a debug build on 32 threads locally; one thread in release 14.7 ms p50 / 16.4 p95 (out-of-tree probe). Every tile awake (simulation/matter-1024-dense, 42 ms debug, about 16 ms release on 16 threads) is the device kernel's, which is the CPU's bits (T1.8)

budgets.name: simulation/rigid-pyramid-20
budgets.why: T2.9, D-176: the rigid family is Box2D v3 under our contract, so its speed is Box2D's — the same 211 bodies stepped 240 times on a World and on Box2D called directly, in the same run and taking turns, every body at the same place in both: 1.6% over locally (2.85 ms against 2.81); the limit leaves room for a shared runner's noise

budgets.name: simulation/rigid-rain-1000
budgets.why: T2.9: the same with 1000 boxes and circles falling into a pile, where the contact list the World gathers after each step is longest: 3.4% over locally (45.9 ms against 44.4 for 240 steps)

budgets.name: render/scene-extract-10k
budgets.why: M6.3: what a view sees of 10,000 instances with every instance looked at — culled, sorted, batched (3,836 draws in 288 batches): 2.8 ms p95 in a debug build locally (270 ns an instance); it is the reference the tree's path is held to, and a frame's budget for the scene's part is a millisecond in a release build

budgets.name: render/scene-extract-10k
budgets.why: AGENTS §4: a steady frame's extraction is written into what the last frame left

budgets.name: render/scene-extract-10k-tree
budgets.why: M6.3: the same draws by the scene's tree, 4,089 of the 10,000 looked at: 2.2 ms p95 in a debug build locally; the sort of the draws is most of what is left

budgets.name: render/scene-extract-10k-tree
budgets.why: AGENTS §4: the walk's stack is on the stack

budgets.name: render/scene-follow-10k
budgets.why: M6.3: the mirror following a frame in which 100 of 10,000 instances moved — the tree's boxes refitted, its shape kept; after 64 refits a new tree is made beside it 4,096 things a frame and takes its place, so no frame makes the whole tree (a debug build locally, 2026-11-14: median 0.63 ms, p95 1.43 ms, p99 1.95 ms, the largest 2.8 ms — where the whole tree every 64th frame was 34 ms)

budgets.name: render/scene-follow-10k
budgets.why: D-187: no frame of following a moving scene of 10,000 things is over a 120th of a second (it was 31 ms when the tree was made again whole)

budgets.name: render/mesh-reference-yard
budgets.why: M6.3, D-184: the CPU reference of the mesh pass — 6,092 triangles, 480x270, five outputs a pixel, one thread: 3.2 ms p50 locally (31 ns a pixel; the package builds at -O2), 15.7 ms p95 on a machine doing other work. A reference is held to its bits, not to a frame; the bound is there so that a change that makes it several times dearer is seen

budgets.name: render/mesh-reference-yard
budgets.why: AGENTS §4: a frame into targets of the same size allocates nothing (what it remembers of the last frame is kept)

budgets.name: render/mesh-reference-glow
budgets.why: M6.3: the CPU reference of the glow — 480x270, six box passes of 15 texels each summed afresh (exact, not a running sum), one thread: 4.7 ms p50, 4.8 ms p95 locally (37 ns a pixel). A reference; the bound is there so that a change that makes it several times dearer is seen

budgets.name: render/mesh-reference-glow
budgets.why: AGENTS §4: its working space is kept between frames

budgets.name: simulation/world-128x64-frame
budgets.why: M6.2: one frame of a whole 2D world the size of a showcase's cavern — the lattice, what flies, the coupling, the rigid step — with a fire about it: 0.75 ms p95 optimised locally (84 ns a cell; the lattice 95% of it, the terrain's collision 4%, the rest under 1%); a playtest that branches ahead pays this thousands of times, and four times it is a quarter of a 60 Hz frame

budgets.name: simulation/world-128x64-frame
budgets.why: AGENTS §4: a frame of the world allocates nothing (the coupling's scratch is kept between frames)

budgets.name: simulation/world-128x64-branch
budgets.why: D-169: a branch of the whole world — a timeline's snapshot, an agent's `world.branch` before a frame is run — is a copy of the field and the rigid world from its own image: 0.09 ms p95 locally (38 allocations: a branch's world in one reserved block is mlibs.memory's to give, when branching by the ten thousand asks for it)

budgets.name: simulation/matter-256-shade
budgets.why: D-168 worst case: every cell of 256x256 of the standard matter shaded by the standard appearance — a row's base, its grain, nine tints, the light — and both images updated: 4.9 ms p95 in a debug build locally (71 ns a cell); a step changes far fewer tiles, and a pack change or a load is bounded by this

budgets.name: simulation/matter-lattice-256-sparse
budgets.why: D-167: a sparse step of matter allocates nothing

budgets.name: simulation/matter-lattice-256-sparse
budgets.why: T1.7: 256x256 of the standard matter with cells that move — a basin of water that does not rest and a fire along wood keep 19 of 64 tiles awake: 15.7 ms p95 in a debug build locally with the standard definition's 9 channels and 19 laws (790 ns a cell run, 19456 of 65536; 11.8 ms with its 7 channels and 14 laws at T1.7); a first bound, the device's kernel is the path for a world this size all awake

budgets.name: dynamics/softbody-24
budgets.why: D-133: a soft body's step reuses its working space (a UI's figure, Mui, steps it every frame it moves)

budgets.name: dynamics/softbody-24
budgets.why: D-133: a figure's softness in a frame's budget — 8 substeps of a 24-particle ring (0.017 ms p95 in a debug build locally, 690 ns a particle); a first bound, measured against rivals in P1

budgets.name: dynamics/softbody-96
budgets.why: D-133: the same at 96 particles

budgets.name: simulation/checkpoint-64
budgets.why: the shared timeline owns preallocated fixed-shape snapshots; one step including a checkpoint reuses capacity

budgets.name: public-motion/scoped-program-seek-100x2
budgets.why: Prepared nested scopes sample and publish with their geometry on the shared zero-allocation player path

budgets.name: public-motion/image-bindings-resolve-64
budgets.why: 64 prepared effect schemas resolve sampled parameters and defaults into caller storage without per-frame allocation; renderer execution excluded

budgets.name: public-motion/program-seek-100x2
budgets.why: 100 independent instances of one nested two-track three-segment preparation reuse track-max double buffers across arbitrary phase-crossing seeks; preparation/rendering excluded

budgets.name: public-motion/engine-advance-500
budgets.why: 500 public object playback plans plus effect parameters reuse prepared double buffers during native batch advance; setup excluded, no renderer or whole-frame claim

budgets.name: public-motion/object-query-500
budgets.why: owned capture and prepared name/ref/resource queries must reuse existing storage: 500 complete public object query batches per iteration, after setup and harness warmup; this is not an Engine or whole-frame budget

budgets.name: ui/presentation/publish-100
budgets.why: 100 preselected local transform offsets publish atomically through warmed UI channel leases without allocation; excludes Engine sampling, painting and rendering

budgets.name: ui/presentation/hanim-frame-100
budgets.why: prepared public Hanim transport, 100 card parts and the warmed 302-node Runtime paint frame reuse storage; ordinary C++ allocations counted, raster/GPU excluded

budgets.name: ui/presentation/hanim-effects-frame-100
budgets.why: prepared effect bindings, publication, Runtime paint and content bounds reuse buffers with all fixed-size glyph subpixel masks prepared; cold glyph generation, new text/sizes and raster/filter/GPU execution excluded

budgets.name: ui/frame/one-label
budgets.why: M1 acceptance ⑤: a 1000-node interface at 1080p on the CPU renderer holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: ui/frame/hover-sweep
budgets.why: pointer motion over the same interface holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: ui/frame/all-labels
budgets.why: even when every label of the interface changes in one frame

budgets.name: ui/frame/animate-all
budgets.why: a strong-animation framework (D-60): every card of the interface in motion still holds 60 Hz

budgets.name: canvas/sharpen
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §3.5: after the camera stops, what is on screen is sharp again within 300 ms

budgets.name: canvas/pan-1000
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §3.5: panning a wall of 1000 windows costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame (raster aside)

budgets.name: canvas/zoom-sweep-1000
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §3.5: zooming the same wall in and out costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame

budgets.name: canvas/pan-100k
budgets.why: the grid index: a 100,000-node scene pans as cheaply as what is on screen

budgets.name: wall/zoom-sweep-1000
budgets.why: S1 (canvas-markdown §3.5): a zoom sweep 1% ↔ 400% over 1000 pages costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame; nodes go live when the camera rests

budgets.name: wall/pan-1000
budgets.why: S1: panning 1000 pages drawn as textures costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame

budgets.name: wall/workspace-drag-100
budgets.why: S1: a workspace of 100 windows dragged by its label (a declarative behaviour) costs under 1 ms a frame

budgets.name: wall/selection-drag-1000
budgets.why: S1: 1000 chosen windows dragged together, with snapping and the minimap, cost under 1 ms a frame

budgets.name: wall/stream-20
budgets.why: S1 (§3.4): 20 windows written into at 50 tokens a second drop no frame at 120 Hz

budgets.name: wall/sharpen
budgets.why: S1 (§3.5): after the camera stops over a wall of pages, every window on screen is sharp within 300 ms

budgets.name: canvas-kit/drag-100k
budgets.why: canvas-markdown §1.1: dragging a selection with snapping, the grid and a minimap of 100,000 nodes costs under 1 ms of CPU a frame

budgets.name: glass/10-1080p-cpu
budgets.why: the CPU reference of liquid glass (D-64) stays a usable preview: ten panels over a 1080p frame in bands on the task pool (about 110 ms on CI's four cores); real-time glass is the GPU's

budgets.name: render/mesh-device-yard-1080p
budgets.why: D-187: the whole frame of three dimensions at 1080p — occlusion, three lights' shadow maps, light, glow, tone — at 120 frames a second on a GPU (2.6 ms mean on an RTX 4080, 2026-11-14)

budgets.name: render/mesh-device-yard-1080p
budgets.why: a frame on a device allocates nothing: the command list keeps its room, and so does the backend

budgets.name: render/mesh-device-tiles-1080p
budgets.why: D-187: a textured floor to the horizon at 1080p — up to eight places of a pixel's strip, each one read of the texture's levels (mlibs.rhi's TextureDesc::levels) — at 120 frames a second on a GPU

budgets.name: render/mesh-device-tiles-1080p
budgets.why: a frame on a device allocates nothing

budgets.name: glass/10-1080p-gpu
budgets.why: D-64 and M4: ten glass panels over a 1080p frame at 120 Hz on a GPU (a software device, as CI's lavapipe, is reported, not held to it)

budgets.name: wall/zoom-sweep-1000-gpu
budgets.why: S1 (§19.3): 1000 windows swept from 1% to 400% at 120 Hz, frame p99 under 8.3 ms, the GPU drawing every frame

budgets.name: wall/zoom-sweep-1000-gpu-lists
budgets.why: D-187, D-188 (plan §5.9 step a): the same sweep with the windows' content as lists under the camera — every primitive where it is at every zoom, nothing stretched — held to the same frame

budgets.name: render/arrive-page-gpu
budgets.why: D-187 (plan §5.9 step c): the frame new content enters in — a 1080p page of 26 thousand glyphs over four thousand cards the renderer has not seen, encoded and drawn within a 120 Hz frame (3.2 ms on an RTX 4080 with the frame's own glyph run, 30.6 ms a primitive each)

budgets.name: render/arrive-page-gpu-kept
budgets.why: the same page as a kept run of a new revision each frame: its glyphs made for the device and sent in the frame it arrives in (3.3 ms on an RTX 4080)

budgets.name: motion/switches-100
budgets.why: universal motion (D-93): a hundred switches flipped at once, every frame of their morphs drawn at 1080p by the CPU — 4.5 ms on CI's four cores (1.3 locally, 2026-11-02), a third of a 60 Hz frame

budgets.name: motion/switches-100-liquid
budgets.why: the same with liquid's merging drops on the CPU reference (37 ms on CI's four cores, 11 locally) — metaball runs from T3, where a GPU draws it (the -gpu budget); this one holds the reference from getting slower

budgets.name: motion/switches-100-ink
budgets.why: the same with ink's wavering line on the CPU reference (74 ms on CI's four cores, 35 locally) — wobble runs from T2, where a GPU draws it (the -gpu budget); this one holds the reference from getting slower

budgets.name: motion/switches-100-ink-gpu
budgets.why: ink's hundred switches where they run: the GPU draws each frame within 120 Hz

budgets.name: motion/switches-100-liquid-gpu
budgets.why: liquid's hundred switches where they run: the GPU draws each frame within 120 Hz

budgets.name: render/effect-wobble

budgets.name: render/effect-metaball

budgets.name: render/effect-neon

budgets.name: render/effect-paper

budgets.name: ui/frame/hover-sweep

budgets.name: ui/frame/idle

budgets.why: building and laying out the whole interface fits in one frame

budgets.why: shaping and breaking stay well under a microsecond and a half per byte

budgets.why: a Markdown answer parses at 25 MB/s or more: a 40 KB document in under 2 ms (about 10 ns per byte measured)

budgets.name: markdown/stream-token

budgets.name: markdown/to-html
budgets.why: copy as HTML of a long answer stays below a millisecond

budgets.name: text/glyph-motion
budgets.why: styling a glyph for a frame of motion stays far below its rasterisation: 2 000 animated glyphs cost under a millisecond

budgets.name: render/gradient-fill-1080p-linear
budgets.why: a ramp of gentle steps is one read of the table a pixel on the CPU reference: 2.2 ns a pixel measured on the development machine, the margin a shared CI runner's

budgets.name: render/gradient-fill-1080p-linear-steep
budgets.why: a steep ramp's colour between two entries (plan §5.9 gap 6) is two multiplications a pixel more: 3.2 ns measured

budgets.name: render/gradient-fill-1080p-radial
budgets.why: a radial gradient a pixel at a time, a square root each: 4.6 ns measured

budgets.name: render/gradient-fill-1080p-radial-steep

budgets.name: render/effect-particles
budgets.why: the CPU reference of a particle burst stays interactive: a 480 × 320 layer under 10 ms (the GPU path is the fast one)

budgets.name: trace/span-off
budgets.why: tracing that is off is a branch on a relaxed load (D-59): a few cycles even on a shared CI runner, so a frame's spans cost under a microsecond

budgets.name: trace/span-on
budgets.why: recording a span takes no lock and no allocation (D-59)

budgets.name: log/filtered-out
budgets.why: a log record the filter leaves out is not formatted (D-59): a branch on a relaxed load, a few cycles even on a shared CI runner

budgets.name: gongfu/frame
budgets.why: D-85 §8.6: a frame of the fighting game's simulation is a rounding error of the frame (about 1 µs measured), so rollback never competes with drawing

budgets.name: gongfu/frame
budgets.why: D-85: the match state is one block of plain data; a frame of simulation allocates nothing

budgets.name: audio/automated-mix
budgets.why: 128 frames are 2.67 ms at 48 kHz; 48 voices plus prepared scalar automation must fit within a fifth of that callback interval

budgets.name: audio/automated-mix
budgets.why: the sample-clock adapter owns its prepared keys and reuses the mixer's block scratch; no hot-loop allocation

budgets.name: audio/mix-48
budgets.why: D-86: a block of 128 frames (2.67 ms of sound at 48 kHz) with 48 voices, an echo and the limiter in under a fifth of the time it lasts (about 0.045 ms measured)

budgets.name: audio/mix-48
budgets.why: the audio thread allocates nothing: a sound's tables are made when it is added

budgets.name: gongfu/rollback-8
budgets.why: D-85 §8.6: eight frames rolled back and played again (each state saved) cost under 16 µs, a thousandth of a 60 Hz frame (about 90 ns a frame measured)

budgets.name: gongfu/rollback-8
budgets.why: a rollback restores bytes and simulates again: nothing allocated

budgets.name: gongfu/present2d
budgets.why: building a frame's picture of two skeletons and their effects is a small part of a 120 Hz frame (about 30 µs measured)

budgets.name: breakout/step
budgets.why: mgame S4 design: a step of the breakout (about 13 balls among 96 bricks, each swept) is a small part of its 8.3 ms at 120 Hz (about 0.013 ms measured at p95)

budgets.name: breakout/step
budgets.why: the breakout's state is one block of plain data: a step allocates nothing

budgets.name: breakout/seek
budgets.why: a rewind is a snapshot copied and at most 59 steps again: well inside a frame (6 % of one at most), so holding R rewinds smoothly; 0.43 ms measured at p95 on CI's runner with the five rooms' state

budgets.name: breakout/seek
budgets.why: the timeline's snapshots and inputs are rings made when it starts: seeking allocates nothing

budgets.name: gongfu/present2d
budgets.why: D-85 §8.4: a picture is a pure function of the state, drawn by a Painter that reuses its poses and paths: nothing allocated each frame

budgets.name: public-motion/shape-sample-500

budgets.name: public-motion/paint-sample-record-500
budgets.why: the public prepared material sampling/recording contract: 500 sixteen-leaf sample calls plus 500 arena record calls reuse warmed caller storage with no heap allocation; the exact official release workload was measured at zero
